findings.text: The status treats 200 lines as a limit on the proof, but the workspace stop rule applies only to work missing from the task, and the task already identifies these proof obligations. Fix: Keep the estimates and mark the proof as pending unless a specific unplanned requirement triggers the stop rule.

The account of the view proof omits `run.sourceCertain = true`, which `QuerySource.join` checks even when the subquery has no fault and ends with `.done`. Fix: Include the whole-row certainty obligation and discharge it from the view’s zero offset and absent limit.

The proposed general law assumes equal step outputs suffice for preservation, but `sendStatements_single_observations` also requires `resolved.fromQuery = false` before and after the migration to exclude alternative executions of the observed statement. Fix: State both resolution premises or specialize the law to a single `SELECT` and discharge them there.

The comment promises a load-independent answer, but a loaded runner can still exhaust the 60-second compiled-work budget and return `unknown`, failing the test that expects `false`. Fix: Describe the larger budget as reducing the risk of a timeout and remove the guarantee.
